newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba to crack down on abettors of prostitution.
newsitem.headline: Cuba to crack down on abettors of prostitution.

text.p: A Cuban law that goes into effect next month sets stiff fines, prison sentences and confiscation of property for pimps, madams and those who rent space out for prostitution.

An article in Sunday's Juventud Rebelde newspaper said that under a law on vice approved by the Cuban National Assembly late last month, punishment will be meted out "not to the person who sells his or her body but to those who benefit by it or who contribute in some way to others prostituting themselves."

As an example, the article said that somebody who rented his or her house out to be used for prostitution "can receive a jail sentence of from two to five years, fines and possibly confiscation of property."
If the accused works in the field of public health, education, tourism, law enforcement or government, the sentence can be increased to eight years, the weekly said.

The law also calls for prison sentences of up to eight years for those found guilty of using threats or blackmail to force unwilling people to take part in sexual acts. The same maximum sentence is prescribed for those who take sexual advantage of children under 16 in their care or the mentally or physically disabled.
The law goes into effect at the end of August, the newspaper said.
